title: The same ruins, today
story: The same ruins a century and a half later: a public park, a walking path, the carved stonework fenced and open to the sky.

title: Temple of Heaven
story: The Temple of Heaven in the 1910s, from a stereograph view sold to foreign visitors. The compound had been the emperor's stage for the harvest rites for nearly five hundred years.

title: Street traffic at Qianmen
story: Traffic just south of the Zhengyangmen gate, around 1905. This is Qianmen street, and it is still a shopping street today.

title: The south wall of the Inner City
story: Beijing's city wall around 1900-1903, photographed from the southeast. Most of the walls were dismantled in the decades that followed; this line survives as a street.

title: The Lama Temple
story: The great Tibetan Buddhist monastery around 1900. A century and a half earlier the Qianlong emperor had lived here as a boy prince, before his father took the throne.
credit: Chandless collection, Wikimedia Commons, public domain

title: Zhengyangmen, the southern gate
story: The main southern gate of the Inner City, photographed around 1900. The streets around it burned that year during the Boxer uprising; the gate tower was rebuilt soon after and still stands at the head of Qianmen street.

title: Summer Palace, general view
story: The Summer Palace around 1890, newly rebuilt along Kunming Lake for the court of the Empress Dowager. The same shoreline is a public park today.
credit: Detroit Publishing Co., Wikimedia Commons, public domain

title: Marco Polo Bridge
story: Thomas Child photographed the Marco Polo Bridge in 1877, its carved stone lions already centuries old. The bridge crosses the Yongding River at the city's southwest approach.
credit: Thomas Child, Wikimedia Commons, public domain

title: Ruins of the European Palaces
story: Thomas Child at the ruins of the European Palaces, built for the Qianlong emperor and burned by Anglo-French forces in 1860. He photographed the wreckage barely a decade later.
credit: Thomas Child, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
